ultrasonography is useful in the evaluation of cancerous pleural and chest invasion of lung cancer, and that the accuracy is high, especially for the most critical grade of the invasion, that is, grade 3.
ultrasonographic findings can be used to accurately assess cancerous invasion into pleura and chest walls of patients with lung cancers.
the ultrasonographic classification of lung cancer invasion of the pleura and the chest wall was useful in staging patients with lung cancer.

the evaluation of pleural invasion of lung cancer, using ultrasonography.
the development of a new approach to the study of the effects of the invasion on the chest wall in patients.
the ultrasonographic classification of cancerous invasion of the pleura and the chest wall, and the evaluation of the ultrasonographic method for the staging of lung cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the accuracy of ultrasonographic evaluation of lung cancer is comparable with computed tomographic evaluation, and that the ultrasonographic evaluation is superior in the detection of chest wall invasion and in the assessment of pleural invasion, particularly in the early stages.
the accuracy of ultrasonography in evaluation of the invasion of lung cancer was comparable to that of CT, and that ultrasonography was superior to CT in evaluation of uP-3.

ultrasonography is a useful tool in evaluating cancer invasion into the pleural and chest walls, which is important for staging of patients with primary lung cancer and for decisions on surgical intervention.

the use of ultrasonography in the evaluation of cancer invasion into the pleural space and chest wall is a useful tool for staging lung cancer and planning treatment.
